newsitem.title: USA: Conn. legislators seek to stop gasoline tax--paper.
newsitem.headline: Conn. legislators seek to stop gasoline tax--paper.

text.p: Connecticut legislators said they planned to try to stop the latest increase in gasoline taxes that is set to go into effect on January 1, the Hartford Courant said in its Tuesday edition.
The state's gasoline taxes, which the paper said were the highest in the nation, have risen every 90 days since October 1995, and are set to hit 39 cents per gallon at the start of 1997.
During the past legislative session, lawmakers were unable to derail the tax increase.
Gov. John Rowland also plans to call for a cut in the gasoline taxes when he announces his new budget proposal in February.
And starting on Tuesday, the gross receipts tax on hospital bills, will fall to 9.25 percent from 11 percent, saving hospitals $26 million in the 1996-97 fiscal year.
This tax is set to fall on October 1 each year until it hits 6.25 percent in 1999, the paper said.
